correctness.rationale: The reflected-switching generator yields coupled Poisson and harmonic backward systems with mixed Dirichlet-Neumann conditions. Reflection-and-gate exchange reduce them to one parabola and a sinh mode for the mean and to an affine function and a cosh mode for left absorption. Boundary equations give explicit constants; the all-position Robin mean forces equal endpoint reactivities and fixes h_time=D*alpha*coth(t), whereas the exact split fixes h_split=D*alpha*tanh(t), a strict difference for every t>0. A uniform killing minorization gives finite expectation and uniqueness. Independent finite-state matrix checks passed 24 joint cases; finite tests are not used as proof.

value.rationale: Mean escape time and side-specific capture frequencies are independently measurable observables for intermittently gated transport. The strict exactly computable calibration factor coth^2(t)>1 is a sharp structural obstruction to replacing the natural two-gate system by a static local radiation boundary, not merely a routine boundary-value solve. The discrepancy vanishes in a fast-switching limit, providing a motivated physical boundary on coarse graining.
